record.title: TierKV combines predictive KV-cache compression and flash tiers for mobile LLM inference
record.summary: Shu et al. describe TierKV, an accepted EuroSys 2027 system that predicts cache demand from prefill states and jointly places tokens in exact, low-rank and flash-offloaded tiers. In the authors’ eight-model, three-mobile-SoC evaluation, it reduced RAM-resident KV cache by 12.5–34% and improved prefill throughput by up to 17.6× versus MNN-LLM; the largest speedup is baseline-specific. Average end-to-end speedup was 1.10× versus llama.cpp, while decoding throughput fell in some cases from SVD reconstruction. These are paper-reported results; no independent reproduction was performed.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The arXiv v2 paper identifies TierKV as an accepted EuroSys 2027 paper and describes a predictive three-tier KV-cache system for mobile LLM inference.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across eight text, vision and audio models on three mobile SoCs, the authors report reducing RAM-resident KV-cache footprint by 12.5–34%; maximum supported context length increases by up to 2.6× in the tested memory regime.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper reports prefill throughput improvements up to 17.6× over MNN-LLM for selected text models and an average end-to-end speedup of 1.10× over llama.cpp across evaluated workloads; decoding throughput decreases in some cases due to SVD reconstruction.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper does not establish these gains on other device families, models, workloads or independent implementations; its maximum prefill gain is not a general end-to-end speedup.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of the system, speed, memory or accuracy measurements was conducted.
Cross-device generality and behavior under realistic prompt-length distributions, thermal throttling and competing storage/memory load remain uncertain.

brief.importance_rationale: If replicated across representative mobile workloads, reducing KV-cache memory while preserving long-context access could materially expand on-device inference capability and privacy-preserving deployment. The reported results are bounded to the tested models and SoCs, with baseline-dependent speedups and no independent implementation audit.
limitations: Author-reported system measurements; no independent implementation audit or reproduction was performed.
The maximum 17.6× prefill throughput comparison is against MNN-LLM on selected workloads; average end-to-end improvement over llama.cpp is 1.10×.
Comparisons are incomplete where baseline frameworks do not support the same model or long-context regime.
SVD reconstruction lowers decode throughput in some cases; prefill gains do not imply faster decoding in every workload.
Device results are limited to three evaluated mobile SoCs; thermal throttling and external validity remain concerns.
brief.summary: Shu et al. describe TierKV, an accepted EuroSys 2027 system that predicts cache demand from prefill states and jointly places tokens in exact, low-rank and flash-offloaded tiers. In the authors’ eight-model, three-mobile-SoC evaluation, it reduced RAM-resident KV cache by 12.5–34% and improved prefill throughput by up to 17.6× versus MNN-LLM; the largest speedup is baseline-specific. Average end-to-end speedup was 1.10× versus llama.cpp, while decoding throughput fell in some cases from SVD reconstruction. These are paper-reported results; no independent reproduction was performed.

technical.claimed_result: The authors evaluate eight text, vision and audio models on three mobile SoCs. They report 12.5–34% lower resident KV-cache memory, up to 17.6× prefill throughput versus MNN-LLM in selected cases, and 1.10× average end-to-end speedup versus llama.cpp; SVD reconstruction reduces decoding throughput in some configurations.
technical.compute_or_cost: The framework adds approximately 10k lines of C/C++/OpenCL and Python according to the paper. One-time per-model calibration uses two A6000 GPUs and is reported as under 20 minutes.
technical.demonstrated_result: The accepted EuroSys 2027 paper (arXiv:2609.21172v2) and its method, platform, baselines, tables and accuracy/multi-turn results were inspected. Reported measurements were not independently reproduced.
technical.implementation_status: Research system described in an accepted EuroSys 2027 paper; implementation and results are author-reported. Code was not inspected or run in this activation.
technical.mechanism: Before decoding, Predictive Multi-Tier Cache Optimization uses prefill hidden states to estimate sequence demand and jointly assigns cache tokens to exact, SVD-compressed resident and flash-offloaded tiers under memory and fidelity constraints.
technical.regime: Eight models across text, image and audio workloads on Adreno 740/750 and Mali-G715 mobile SoCs; OnePlus 12 end-to-end comparisons include llama.cpp, MNN-LLM and MLC-LLM where supported.
technical.reproducibility: Evaluation spans eight models and three mobile SoCs; the multi-turn retrieval comparison reports 3 seeds × 5 questions. No independent implementation or replication was conducted.
technical.strongest_baseline: Three mobile inference frameworks are compared, but availability differs by model; MLC-LLM supports only a subset. The reported 17.6× maximum is against MNN-LLM, while the paper reports 1.10× average end-to-end speedup versus llama.cpp.

brief.title: TierKV combines predictive KV-cache compression and flash tiers for mobile LLM inference
brief.why_it_matters: On-device inference is constrained by shared memory and storage bandwidth. Jointly planning compression, cache residency and offload before decoding is a concrete systems approach to longer contexts under fixed device memory, but measured gains depend on the workload and comparator.
